storyInfo: Before the Katorga Incident, Zima is avoiding capture on the Grypherburg outskirts when she takes shelter in a blind elder's home, but she soon realizes the old man's identity is not as simple as it seems—

attributes.text: 'My dear friends, I'm writing this letter as I make my way over...'
'This envelope should reach Deity Grypherburg sooner than I do, if everything goes smoothly. Hopefully, I'll manage to return before New Year's, to celebrate together.'
'After leaving the capital, I went to Zamoresk and Tulskaya. There I learned for the first time how people living next to the capital live, suffer, and die.'
'I joined a few meetings and protests, and even got captured for a few days, but don't worry...'

attributes.content: Creak—!
(Quietly knocks on car door)
attributes.name: Coachman

attributes.content: What's wrong?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: This is as far as I can go. Petrodvorets is just up ahead, and I can see cops waving their flashlights back and forth. Think they're arresting someone.
attributes.name: Coachman

attributes.content: We agreed before we left. I wouldn't put myself in danger.
attributes.name: Coachman

attributes.content: Sure. Tell your kid I say hi. Ivan, right?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: It's alright, child. You paid me, my lips are sealed.
attributes.name: Coachman

attributes.content: Wait, that's not what I meant—
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Winter draws near, and even Petrodvorets across the relatively warm Grypherburg routes cannot escape the biting cold.
Half-withered trees struggle against the strong winds, as branches snap and break alongside fowlbeast cries.
Zima cannot make out any of the lights or sounds the coachman mentioned earlier.
Well, no reason those fat cops would come all the way out here on a night cold enough to freeze a drunk to death.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Now that I'm near the city, I should find somewhere to stay before I work out a way to contact Instructor Dur-nar and get back to Grypherburg...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Zima stuffs her half-written letter into a chest pocket, then steadies herself with a withered tree trunk before continuing on her journey towards the sparsely-lit city in the distance.
Thanks for letting me stay.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: It was your choice to come in.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Yeah, but you didn't chase me away, and even gave me a warm bowl of oatmeal.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Well, did you think I could beat you in a fight?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: 51 Slag Road, huh. I'll pay you back once I make it back to Grypherburg.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Grypherburg? Did you come from the capital?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: You sound young, and talk like a university student. So why come all the way here just to freeze in the cold?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I came here to learn... uh, well, at least I did, at first! There's a lot you don't learn in school, like how to hold a sickle or harvest wheat.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: But it sounds like you weren't really satisfied here either. You're headed home with a gloom about you.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I got mixed up in some things, caused some trouble, and got separated from my friends.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Zima lowers her empty bowl, and wipes her mouth clean with her hand.
I'm still wanted in Tulskaya. I can leave now, if you're worried about that.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Let's not talk about it. Thirty years I've been blind, do you think I can even make out what you look like?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Even if I could, do you think I'd manage to drag these bony legs all the way to the concrete spire in Tulskaya just to compare your mug to the wanted posters on the wall?
attributes.name: Blind Elder
Zima
attributes.content: How do you know that's where they...?

attributes.name: Zima
attributes.content: Huh, guess you were in your prime when they were building the city. I'm sure you've been.
Go wash your bowl, if you're done with your oatmeal.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Zima smoothly scoops snow into the bowl. The oatmeal barely had more flavor than water. Zima easily scrubs it clean.
What did you do?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: You mean in Tulskaya?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Have you committed crimes in other places too?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: No, I'm just... a student.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: At first, I was a guest.
Young thought leaders would share the advanced theories they learned from abroad, and invited me to join their 'little circle'.
They would talk about all sorts of things, confidently state every nation's strengths and evils, as if there was nothing they didn't know.
They were hoping a university student from Grypherburg could help them rally voters and win financial backing.
Until they realized I knew nothing about government, and distanced themselves from me.
So I went to meet workers, doctors, teachers. I wanted to understand their lives, and produce an objective report on their respective situations.
But they would only talk about the weather, traffic, or how many beans they got from a can. They just wouldn't talk about certain topics, and it seemed a habit they grew into.
Even if I could clearly see their pain and apathy.
My luggage was confiscated, my notebook checked from front to back. I knew I couldn't stay any longer.

So I went to the fields. I tried to help some farmers save their wheat from a blizzard, but my pair of hands so used to fighting kept letting grains slip through my fingers, so I wasn't actually much help.
I saw many more suffering. They were experts at enduring their pain, though they didn't know how to verbalize it at all...
They didn't know why it was so difficult to feel joy, nor did they know where their unhappiness came from. They didn't even know who to ask.
I thought about those thought leaders and their theories, their frameworks, their policy plans... none of which could feasibly take root in reality's soil.
Later, I heard students and merchants in the city were organizing a demonstration, although it turned out their true goal was to smuggle and sell weapons from outside... I couldn't figure out why.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Even more confusing was why they gave the authorities my name when they were arrested. I wasn't even in the city at the time!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: What were you doing?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I'd kidnapped a black-hearted taxman.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Alright! Doesn't matter.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Be it the nonsensical politicians, the students who think they know the truth, or ignorant officials, I have zero interest! So enough about them!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Do you think those theories and plans sprouted from themselves, like crops in the soil?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Did you think news from the outside could make its way into Ursus so easily? Do you actually think those students found those 'theories' themselves?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: It is they who control what knowledge you can get. All you know is what they allow you to know!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Remember how they turned your suitcase inside out! That's how they've always treated us!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: So enough!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: You're the one who just started rambling! How about being reasonable?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: If one could be reasonable in Ursus, you wouldn't be here, would you? Go talk to those snotty brats with their nonsensical theories, if you want reason!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: At least they're trying to come up with solutions for the country, instead of sitting at home doing nothing at all.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Do you want to stay here or not?!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: You can't even kick me out—you said so yourself. Not like I'm refusing to pay you either.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Hmph. I'm not one to take empty promises. You want to stay, you help out for the day.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: How?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: See that stack of newspapers by the door? The one who used to read them to me is dead. Do that and you can stay.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Wha...?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Fine.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.text: 'I'm staying in Petrodvorets, at a blind old man's home.'
'His words hint at a unique past, and his accent also sounds a little familiar. I feel like maybe he's from Grypherburg too.'
'Just how many people in Ursus today full of talent and ambition are left to rot in the barrens? It breaks my heart thinking about this.'
'My friends, I promised my journey out of the capital would have me rediscover the country, and I would find a solid, true path amongst all the noise.'
'But now...'

attributes.content: Got today's paper. Want me to read the whole thing?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: No, hold on.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I don't expect you'd want to do that.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Last night. I was ranting, but not without reason.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I can tell you've been through a lot, but I'm not about to pry into your past.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: If only you knew what I've been through—
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I said, I'm NOT going to pry.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I've been to cities around the capital. I've met more people in the past year than I thought I would in a lifetime. Everyone had so much to say.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: And what I've learned... is to see for myself, not just hear from others. I have a habit of looking to the future. I think new will always be better than old.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Hmph. I wasn't planning to tell you anyway!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: What's new... under the sun, then? Read me the paper!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: From the headlines: The State Council's 70th...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: No, none of that Deity Grypherburg Morning News drivel.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Got 'Capital Daily' and 'Journal' here too... no objections? I'll pick one to read from then.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.text: 'A WARNING FROM LONDINIUM? Returnee scholar to give speech on constitutional monarchy.'
\n'FOREIGN MIRACLE, SKYBOUND CITY! The sky is Ursus's way out.'
\n'FORGING FUNDS INTO MIGHT? How wealth always trumps power!'
\n'IMPERIAL COLLEGE REPUTATION AT RISK: Rumor-spreaders will be punished.'
\n'STREET RUFFIANS SUPPRESSED: Ringleader behind street attacks masked as protest march brought to justice.'
\n'TULSKAYA MURDERER FLEES TO OTHER CITIES: Anyone with leads...'

attributes.content: Not gonna talk about any of these?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: What else can I say? Didn't the experts already state their opinion?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Do none of these headlines move you? Can't you feel the fervor of those trying to find a way out for Ursus?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Like this one—
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: 'Far North Miners suffer injustice, inciting uprisings in similarly harsh mining zones for more freedom and quality of life amidst public outrage.'
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Does that mean anything to you? The headline, these people, those miners...?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: It means some die, while others survive.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Nothing worth fussing over.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Then why bother keeping up with the news? Nothing has anything to do with you.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Because I want to know the changes happening across this land. Even if I end up disappointed every day.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: The same old things repeat day in, day out... I wouldn't find anything new, even if I could buy every newspaper printed in this country.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: That's impossible.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Nothing impossible about it. I told you, there's nothing worth your attention.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: 'July 1101, a scholar returned from Victoria developed new views on constitutional monarchy and the parliamentary system through reflection on wartime Londinium...'
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: In January of 1032, a survivor from Gaul presented new ideas on the very same topics based on the battle of the Four Emperors, and even gave a speech at the State Council.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: ...He gave a speech at the State Council...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: One month later he was secretly executed, covered up as an accident.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: ...and was discovered dead in his home this morning, with the cause of death reported to be... an allergic reaction to pollen.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Next, his students and family will flee, then die near the border. Of course, they will now die in accidents related to vehicles powered by Originium instead of burdenbeasts, to keep up with the changing times.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I have older papers beside the wood pile. Feel free to flip through.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I've heard enough.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.text: 'My friends, I've reopened the letter I sealed to add what happened earlier tonight...'
'The blind old man who lives alone has a massive collection of newspapers. He has nearly a century of every kind of paper you can imagine, but this is not what shocked me most.'
'Remember when I told you what I did in the other cities? I was too arrogant then. I had no idea I wasn't the first to commit those acts.'
'Even the comrade mentioned in the papers decades ago wasn't the first to do it.'
'The slogans we yell now have been repeated millions of times over the years; the paths we thought we forged ourselves have long existed, but no one has ever walked their way out!'
'...I'm stumped as to how no one has realized that none of this is new at all.'
'I have a feeling this old man used to be like us...'

attributes.content: Today, university students from seventeen nomadic cities presented a joint petition to the Tsar, demanding improvements to the living conditions of the Infected and more transparency in our mines and their resources.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The issue of the Infected's survival resurfaces on a large scale every ten years or so. You could compile those findings into a book thicker than your average dictionary, but your efforts wouldn't amount to anything.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: It's happened before, after all. Just wait for tomorrow's headlines.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Today, rebels occupied a small town on the border, declaring independence from Ursus. They'll be self-sufficient, and everyone will be treated equally.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: It's happened before. Half of them will die, and the rest will surrender. Wait for tomorrow's paper.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Today, the rebels were beheaded by their own sons, and the remaining rebels formally declared their surrender. In other news, someone has brought back information from Trimounts and is now peddling to the nobility the concept of building up into the skies.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Old news... don't believe me? Look at that paper, from three decades ago. What do you think caused that mysterious explosion in the Northern Tundra?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Wait for tomorrow.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Catastrophe flooded a region... no, don't say anything. I know this isn't new either.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Damn it, I can't find any new news to prove you wrong!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Zima folds the newspaper in her hands, expressions flickering on her face. After a long time, she speaks—
Enough news. I'll talk about what I went through. There's no way what happened to me has happened more than once...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Sounds like you have a unique story for me. Go ahead, if you want.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Do you know... of the Chernobog incident?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: And when was that—
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Five years ago.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: It was winter. Children were forced away from their parents, struggling to survive in one single school, with no food, explanations, or promises...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: No one has any clue what the guy who 'planned' it all was even thinking!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I don't believe something like this has happened before, that it's part of a 'cycle'.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: She forces a smile on her face.
Aha, coming up empty, huh? I win.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: ...Indeed.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: That's the first I've heard of it.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: But you survived, yes?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Huh? No, that's not the point...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Some die, while others survive.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I know things are often more than just a simple label. But sometimes, there is no escaping your most traumatic memories, and that label is all you have.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: What are you trying to say?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Wait for tomorrow.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Hey, come on, tell me—
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: We haven't gotten today's papers yet.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: So let's continue with yesterday's.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Heavy snow's blocked the roads. I'm sure the mailman will deliver them all once the snow's cleared.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Where do I find him?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: You seem more eager than me to read the papers. Why, was there something about the one from yesterday?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I didn't tell you then, but yesterday's paper had a picture of me, with someone else's name on it. A group of students who murdered a noble officer in Tulskaya have fled to this area.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Do you know them?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I don't think so, and besides... they've been killing civilians too.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I need to know where those runaway students fled to... my friends are gonna see my face in the papers, and I'm worried...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Remember to wash your bowl when you're done.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Keep the door closed. I don't want the wind coming in.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: You...?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I'm just blind, not deaf! It doesn't concern me whether you live or die, but you'd best not get buried in the snow... hah, your dirty bowl's still on the table waiting for you to clean it, by the way!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: If there's nothing new in the papers, then don't bring them back, you hear?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: The old man does not wait for a reply before sitting near the door.
This wind... It's too strong!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I gotta find shelter!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Right in front... someone's coming this way?!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Dumb cops haven't noticed us yet... let's keep going.
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Let me rest my legs a little, boss!
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: If you can't walk any longer, I'll go on without you. Hey, what about you? Can you still walk?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Please, don't leave me behind! You promised me you'd help me escape!
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: Escape? I helped you all escape Tulskaya, da? We dodged every guard we saw on our way here, is that not enough?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: You don't even know how to hold a knife properly! Remember, we had to run for our lives through a blizzard because you started a fire and drew the cops over!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Don't forget, we kill the guilty. We're on the side of justice!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: (Pulls on sleeve) Boss...
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: I told you... zip it!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: But boss... there's someone else here...
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: The shocked student with bloody hands turns around to see someone covered in snow trying to hide himself in the shadow of the rock face, with a walking stick in his hand.
Sorry... I just wanted to find somewhere to hide from the wind...
attributes.name: Passer-by Sheltering From The Snow

attributes.content: I'm just here to deliver the papers, look—it's all papers in my bag.
attributes.name: Passer-by Sheltering From The Snow

attributes.content: (Whispering) Boss, there's a wanted notice for us in today's news...
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: No! Stop it! No more killing!
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: What? You're killers?!
attributes.name: Passer-by Sheltering From The Snow

attributes.content: I heard movement over there! Come with me!
attributes.name: Distant Police Officer

attributes.content: The injured student spots the man in the snow open his mouth, as if about to shout something—the next moment, his bloody hands find themselves on the man's neck.
The other male student immediately reacts, wresting the man's stick away.
Please, just... don't make any noise!
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: The passer-by gradually ceases all resistance.
Are those cops gone?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: They're... gone...
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: I think... he's dead.
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: I... killed him?
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: Shut up, idiot!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Listen up, next time it will be you both who do it. I can't always be the one doing the work and taking the blame!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Kasha's almost ready, where's my paper?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: You better not let the snow get you... what a worrisome child.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Oh no, boss! I really can't move any longer!
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: You're so useless! Fine, we'll rest in this battered shack for a bit... Huh? Something's up, I see smoke coming from the chimney.
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: There's someone in there!
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: Who's there? Quiet, or those cops will come over and rob me of all my food!
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Old man, we're hiding from those bastards too. Can we come in for a short break?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Are you not already inside?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Ahem. Quick, close the door.
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: I see two sets of utensils on the table... where's your family gone?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Oh, kid's gone to fetch my papers.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Did you see my kid on your way here?
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Nope, not a single living soul out there.
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Sir... you have so many... newspapers lying around.
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: As you can plainly see, I'm a blind man. All I can do is ask someone else to read the news to me.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: (Whispers) He can't see our faces... can we not kill him—
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: Forgive me for being frank, sir, but what's the point in keeping all of this? It's all lies, and that's the truth!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: I'm just waiting for change to come. You can flip through them as you please... and soon, you'll discover nothing new happens across this land.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: How can that be? I know there are people out there achieving remarkable things!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: There are men out there killing evil nobles and greedy officials alike. No one will dare call the students weak and powerless ever again!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: That's happened before, countless times. Maybe you've all forgotten, but those very same nobles and officials were students at one point in their lives.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: That's not the same! Times have changed, we live in an age of turmoil...
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Every era has its own earth-shaking events.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Hey!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Sir, please... maybe you should rest more and speak less.
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: Heheh, don't worry...
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Fear not, lost youth of today. The kid will probably be back soon, and then I'll ask the town sheriffs to take your group somewhere safe.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: This mountain village is sealed off by the snow. I don't think you'll adapt to the remoteness, you'll fall sick.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Now, do help yourselves to some warm kasha.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: The refugee students' faces turn dark, as the wounded student wipes the sweat on his face with his sleeve, again and again.
(Whispers) Oh no... I think we killed his...
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: (Whispers) Give me that stick.
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: (Whispers) Are you mad? He's gonna know that's his kid's! How are you gonna explain this?
attributes.name: Wounded Student

attributes.content: (Whispers) But why should I... have to explain?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: (Whispers) But... he's just a blind old man...
attributes.name: Worried Student

attributes.content: (Whispers) And how long do you think he'll last in the blizzard without his kid? A whole day? Or half?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Why let a kind soul like him continue to suffer so needlessly?
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: *cough*, *cough*... come on now, kasha's getting cold.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Bloody hands shove the stick into the worried student's hands, as she earns a fierce glare.
Do it!
attributes.name: Runaway Student

attributes.content: Hey, it's me.
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: I found the mailman, he's a nice guy. Said the heavy snow was blocking the roads here, so he brought me to the post office cabin to warm myself up, and even helped contact a truck headed to Grypherburg.
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: If everything goes well, I'll be off to the capital soon!
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: At first, I was worried he'd recognize my face in the papers, but guess what—
attributes.name: Voice Outside the Door

attributes.content: He said, who reads the papers in this day and age? And who would even take them at face value, as truth?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Hello?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Wind from outside rushes in, blowing the newspapers scattered on the ground into the air, like how a baby bothers an adult. Zima looks everywhere, but fails to find the house's elderly occupant.
As she remains in a daze, a second gust of wind snatches the freshly printed newspaper out of her hands, sending its pages wobbling apart until it meshes with the older prints on the floor.
No...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Huh, you're back? Transport's not here yet.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: He wasn't in. Gah, more trouble for everyone. Did you see anyone pass by here?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The mailman shakes his head, and takes a glance at the crumpled newspaper in Zima's hand.
Maybe he found the papers as boring as the ones from yesterday and decided to take a walk.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: How's a blind man going to take a walk in a snowstorm?!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Zima sighs, and tosses the crumpled papers onto the table in front of the mailman.
Anyways, I'll just go look for him, but if you see him... uh, what's that?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Like a squished spring bouncing back, the paper gradually folds open, revealing the front page headline.
Zima had been carrying it the whole time, but this is the first time she has actually read the words on it.
'Petrodvorets Dispatch': Old man living alone murdered in cold blood, killer suspected to be the same fugitive from...
Zima takes to the door at once, but with just a single step, she feels as if a rope is pulling her whole body backwards.
She slowly turns around, fixing her gaze on the nonchalant mailman.
...If this only just happened, how did it end up on the papers so quickly?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: ANSWER ME!!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The mailman stops his work, shrugs at Zima, and replies in a tone she finds all too familiar—
Because it's happened before.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: Everyone who lives here knows it. They don't talk about it, but that doesn't mean they've forgotten.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: The newspaper continues to slowly open on the table, revealing its long-forgotten date to Zima.
That's... today... thirty years ago.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: It's... old news.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The mailman pulls out a letter from his pocket, one resembling the letter Zima has yet to send.
You dropped this.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: How could she have 'dropped' something he literally just took out of his pocket?
The writing...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.text: 'My friends, I fear I can no longer return to Grypherburg.'
'My hands are stained with blood. I used an innocent's walking stick to kill the blind old man who treated us kindly.'
'I've been trying to convince myself with my comrade's words. We had no choice but to kill his son to survive.'
'And how long can an old man who has lost his child even survive on his own? I'm merely helping to minimize the suffering he's going through—this is what I've been telling myself.'
'I almost convinced myself it was true...'
'Until the man's actual son opened the door with skinned quarry and a crossbow in hand...'
'It was then we realized, we had murdered an innocent mailman, and then with arrogance, killed a kind, old man.'
'I ran away... and when I returned, I saw four corpses...'
'I had no clue as to their identities, nor could I tell who was good or bad, I couldn't figure it out...'
'So, I picked up some charcoal and burned my own eyes.'
'My friends, I fear I can no longer return to Grypherburg. I will stay here, and no matter how much time fate grants me, I shall remain here always...'
'Some die, while others survive.'
'I know things are often more than just a simple label. But sometimes, there is no escaping your most traumatic memories, and that label is all you have.'

attributes.content: Oh, you're here.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: We must have missed each other on the way back. You've been gone the whole night, so I went out to look for you.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Well, now that you're here, I'm at ease. It's time I head back.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Wait.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The roads here are rough, but you're completely fine? Have you... walked this path before?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Every time I think about the past, I take a walk on this path.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: It doesn't matter that I can't see, or even if I fall. Falling only means I have to be more careful of rocks and potholes next time.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Fall enough times, take enough beatings, and you'll naturally manage to walk steadily on the right path.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: I guess you were right. This has all happened before.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I told you so.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: But that doesn't mean I'm wrong.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The weather will change, and so will the roads. After all, these roads were paved by the ones who first walked here, step by step.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Your knees are all muddy. You've walked this path your whole life and yet you still fell today. Right?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I can't even see, so say whatever you want.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Ahem, I can testify... that I do see traces of mud.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: I still believe every new day will be different from the last, even if it's by the tiniest bit. It's still a victory worth celebrating.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Maybe these small changes aren't enough to build a bridge, maybe it's hard for those experiences and theories from abroad to take root here, but to quote something you said before—
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The path to the future that belongs to Ursus will surely grow from Ursus's own soil. Maybe it'll sprout today, or tomorrow...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: But never yesterday!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I don't think that's how I put it... fine. Seems like I was right again.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Zima scoops a pile of snow from outside, carefully rubbing it into the elder's numb hands.
I have to head back to Grypherburg, so I don't think I can wash that bowl clean. Sorry.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Any news you want me to bring back to the capital?
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: The blind elder shakes his head, avoiding Zima's question, but changes his tone.
An ant trapped in a circle drawn with chalk naturally cannot make what's outside it, but if you can—
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: A truck honks its horn from outside the post office's wooden hut, as if urging them to hurry. The old man has no choice but to switch his words into those of a farewell.
I hope you will manage to forge a brand new path of your own.
attributes.name: Blind Elder

attributes.content: Time to go!
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: Right, if you haven't read today's papers yet, there's something you ought to know...
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: Those murdering students? They accidentally ate some poisonous berries because they were starving, and were sent to the hospital by some kind-hearted people. Then they got arrested.
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: Seems like sometimes things don't happen exactly as they did back then, huh?
attributes.name: Mailman

attributes.content: Istina, Leto, Gummy, Natalya, Zoya. I'll soon be back in Grypherburg.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Those who bet that I wouldn't return before the new year better prepare their cupcakes for me, because I'm starving!
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Before I left the capital, I told Instructor Dur-nar that all the hardships I'd meet on this trip would be worth it if it managed to truly open my eyes to our motherland.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Looking back, I think it was worth it. If I were to use the big words and terms I learned in university to phrase my feelings, then this is how I'd put it—
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Our homeland is trapped in a cycle, where suffering, ignorance, and evil propagate in unison, while our so-called hope is but a hollow prize to claim. This system only continues to function because we continue to endure it.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: I've seen countless people try to transplant paths from other nations, or put a stake on current sentiments, which I used to think was the safest way to do it.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: But after going through some stuff, I realized that's just part of the cycle too. The abyss of history is littered with those failures.
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: But failure is also fertile ground for answers to take root. The path to the future that belongs to Ursus will surely grow from Ursus's own soil...
attributes.name: Zima

attributes.content: Zima stops her pen when she seems to hear bells tolling all the way from nearby Grypherburg. The capital's silhouette lies right before her eyes.
The Winter Ball will begin in a few days. And right now, the Student Assembly's meeting is already underway.
So she tears the letter to shreds, tossing it into the snow. In the end, the bookish tone she ended up writing proved too corny for her taste, but this is not exactly why she trashes it.
She decides, she will say the very same words to her companions in person. No, she won't even have to say them.
I'll break this cycle with my own hands.
attributes.name: Zima
